implementation_notes: Default Java realization: declare the service interface, list implementations in META-INF/services/<interface> (or a provides directive in module-info.java) and let ServiceLoader.load find, cache and instantiate them; the loader is the registry and the class path is the discovery medium. It replaces explicit registration code, at the cost of no runtime registration and no keyed lookup - providers are found by type, and callers must index them by their own key.
pitfalls: ServiceLoader instantiates lazily during iteration and caches the result, so relocating or adding JARs after load is not reflected (reload() clears the cache).
Providers must have a public no-argument constructor; Kotlin objects and classes hiding their constructor cannot be loaded directly, so a generated or hand-written proxy class is required.
Duplicates are ignored silently and iteration order follows class-path/JAR order, which is not stable across environments - never make behaviour depend on provider order.

variants.name: ConcurrentHashMap registry class
variants.implementation_notes: The in-process mutable registry: a ConcurrentHashMap (or a Map wrapped with Collections.synchronizedMap) keyed by String, with register using putIfAbsent for fail-fast duplicates and lookup using get; entries are usually suppliers so creation stays lazy. Choose it when registration happens at runtime or the key is data, not a type.
pitfalls: computeIfAbsent must not update the same map inside its mapping function - ConcurrentHashMap detects the recursive update and throws IllegalStateException.
Iteration over ConcurrentHashMap is weakly consistent: a registry listing can miss concurrent registrations, which matters for diagnostics but not for lookup.
ConcurrentHashMap rejects null keys and values, so optional or placeholder registrations must be modelled another way (never with null).
